searchText: As I mentioned it earlier, it might be worth briefly talking about separately: The current plan at least for our AA MVP is to have AA contracts be normal contracts with a fixed code prefix that asserts the contract was called from a special `ENTRY_POINT` address. We are for now working with the prefix mentioned above: > which is > `0x3373ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff14601e57600080fd5b` I have also written a little tool to inject that prefix into any contract creation bytecode, which effectively turns the deployed contract into an AA test contract: https://github.com/adietrichs/aa-tools The tool basically injects the prefix at the beginning of the contract code and fixes all resulting `JUMPDEST` offset problems. It is obviously purely for testing purposes - before AA ever reaches mainnet we would have proper support for it directly in Solidity. But if you replace the `ENTRY_POINT` address with one you control, you can already play around with the tool and see it working on-chain 🙂 Besides that I have just written up a short list of some of the open questions around AA that we as Quilt have been discussing internally: https://hackmd.io/@KuiKHwIPT4e8_VWfnKLHvw/Byd91DvKI Always happy about feedback! I think we will probably start sharing more of our progress here in this channel as our MVP implementation in geth is coming along. I propose something like: ``` CALLER GETPC ADD PUSH1 0x1e ; Needs to be updated JUMPI ``` Instead of the current AA check. _laughs in codegolf._ interesting, probably something we would do for production, "find the shortest / cheapest bytecode sequence with the same effect" Hm, nope. obv. the second part (revert if no jump and then the jumpdest) is missing, and you would have to adjust the jump target - but apart from that it should work Address is 160 bits, wraps at 256 ah, good point well, nice try then 😉 We might have to change the prefix anyway though, to allow for incoming ETH transfers > https://hackmd.io/@KuiKHwIPT4e8_VWfnKLHvw/Byd91DvKI I think I mention that in here. Also still not sure if the prefix is even the way to go, but of course for the MVP we will stick to it. > which is > `0x3373ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff14601e57600080fd5b` <@415548822983278593> Why not `PUSH1 2 PUSH1 160 EXP PUSH1 1 SUB`? Fewer bytes Or I think `PUSH1 2 PUSH1 160 EXP NEG NOT` works too and is a byte shorter Oh oh `PUSH1 32 DUP EXP NEG NOT` 🤣 cheapest for 160bits of ones: `0 NOT 12 SHR` (maybe took the wrong SHR operand order) Aah right SHR got included OK you win And NEG doesn't exist it turns out so mine is 1 longer than youurs 😩 Though `2**160 = 32**32` is a fun coincidence > OK you win :celebrating: If the arg order of SHR was the reverse `PUSH1 12 DUP NOT SHR` would win but it's not 😢 Oh oh `PC NOT PUSH1 12 SHR` OK finally 5 bytes oh its starting at PC=0 (Had no idea what the code is about just jumped in arguing) Any PC under `2**96` would give a correct answer 🤣 Could also use `MSIZE` (just for the fact I'm toying with the idea proposing to remove `PC` opcode) > Any PC under 2**96 would give a correct answer 🤣 Fair point 🙂

I propose something like:

```
CALLER
GETPC
ADD
PUSH1 0x1e  ; Needs to be updated
JUMPI
```

Instead of the current AA check.
